To remove or not to remove? Removal of the unconditional stimulus electrode does not mediate instructed extinction effects
Camilla C. Luck; Ottmar V. Lipp
10.1111/psyp.12452
Crossref abstract only
Abstract Following differential fear conditioning, the instruction that the unconditional stimulus will no longer be presented (instructed extinction) reduces differential electrodermal responding to CS+ and CS−, but does not affect differential conditional stimulus valence evaluations. Reductions in differential electrodermal responding have been attributed to the provision of verbal instructions; however, during instructed extinction the unconditional stimulus electrode is often removed as well. This removal could reduce the participants’ general arousal levels rendering the detection of differential electrodermal responding difficult. decisions.reason: The current source (Luck & Lipp, 2015, Psychophysiology, 10.1111/psyp.12452) is an abstract without in-text citations (full text unavailable), and fresh 0034 reference coding added no named citation. However, the newly supplied primary abstract of shipped row 1519 (Luck & Lipp, 2015, Behaviour Research and Therapy, 10.1016/j.brat.2015.01.001, present in the 26-entry deposited bibliography) establishes a unique compound protocol and finding bridge under Codebook Step 2 (identified_by = description). Shipped row 1519 specifically combined post-conditioning instructed extinction with removal of the shock electrode and tracked continuous self-reported conditional stimulus valence alongside physiological responding, finding that instructed extinction and shock-electrode removal immediately reduced differential fear-potentiated startle and electrodermal responding while conditional stimulus valence resisted instructed extinction. The current study directly tests whether that confounded US electrode removal mediated the physiological effect versus valence resistance by separating instruction/electrode-on, instruction/electrode-off, and non-instructed control groups, empirically retesting both endpoints and confirming that electrodermal responding was eliminated in both instructed groups whereas conditional stimulus valence was unaffected. Other deposited references address general evaluative conditioning, expectancy/affective learning, or emotional extinction expression rather than this compound instructed-extinction plus electrode-removal physiological-versus-valence dissociation. Modifying the design to unconfound electrode removal does not exclude conceptual/procedural retesting. Target_index 0 is therefore already represented by shipped row 1519, without asserting exhaustive knowledge of unseen full-text passages.
